records.title: Toward an internationally accepted standard for reading charts.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Toward an internationally accepted standard for reading charts.
content.abstract: Patients who suffer from sight-threatening eye diseases share a desire to regain a comfortable reading ability. In light of the modern advances achieved in ophthalmic diagnosis and therapy, and because a significant lack of comparability between reading charts still exists, there is an increasing need for a worldwide standard in the form of a norm for diagnostic reading charts. Already, applied advancements such as digital print, which allow a calibration of the print sizes of reading charts in correctly progressing geometric proportions by using the actual height of a lower case "x" in millimeters (x-height), and psychophysically standardizing reading charts and their test items by applying modern statistical methods have significantly contributed to establishing a norm for reading charts. In 2020, a proposal of the British delegation was accepted by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) group "Visual Optics and Optical Instruments," and a working group was established. Bearing in mind the efforts of the ISO with regard to an international norm, this review article is intended to (a) give an overview of the historical background and related normative approaches for diagnostic reading tests used in ophthalmology and optometry, (b) explain psychophysical and technical concerns, and (c) discuss the possibilities and limits of concepts that seem relevant to developing a modern standard for reading charts.

records.title: Size Matters.

content.title: Size Matters.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To describe the ideal size of a laser iridotomy and to discuss its importance.

Design

Perspective.

Methods

Articles in ophthalmology literature on this topic were reviewed, and commentary is provided based on the authors' experiences.

Results

An ideal laser iridotomy size is 200 µm or larger, especially in eyes with uveitis. The final size of an iridotomy must be confirmed after the effects of the pilocarpine has worn off and the pupil is not being constricted by light. A location of the iridotomy furthest from the lid margin may reduce the chances of dysphotopsias and thus allow for an adequate-sized iridotomy.

Conclusions

An iridotomy of an ideal size is needed to reduce the pressure differential on both sides of the iris so as to be effective in eliminating pupillary block.

records.title: Hypotony Failure Criteria in Glaucoma Surgical Studies and Their Influence on Surgery Success.

content.title: Hypotony Failure Criteria in Glaucoma Surgical Studies and Their Influence on Surgery Success.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Review hypotony failure criteria used in glaucoma surgical outcome studies and evaluate their impact on success rates.

Design

Systematic literature review and application of hypotony failure criteria to 2 retrospective cohorts.

Participants

A total of 934 eyes and 1765 eyes undergoing trabeculectomy and deep sclerectomy (DS) with a median follow-up of 41.4 and 45.4 months, respectively.

Methods

Literature-based hypotony failure criteria were applied to patient cohorts. Intraocular pressure (IOP)-related success was defined as follows: (A) IOP ≤ 21 mmHg with ≥ 20% IOP reduction; (B) IOP ≤ 18 mmHg with ≥ 20% reduction; (C) IOP ≤ 15 mmHg with ≥ 25% reduction; and (D) IOP ≤ 12 mmHg with ≥ 30% reduction. Failure was defined as IOP exceeding these criteria in 2 consecutive visits > 3 months after surgery, loss of light perception, additional IOP-lowering surgery, or hypotony. Cox regression estimated failure risk for different hypotony criteria, using no hypotony as a reference. Analyses were conducted for each criterion and hypotony type (i.e., numerical [IOP threshold], clinical [clinical manifestations], and mixed [combination of numerical or clinical criteria]).

Main outcome measures

Hazard ratio (HR) for failure risk.

Results

Of 2503 studies found, 278 were eligible, with 99 studies (35.6%) lacking hypotony failure criteria. Numerical hypotony was predominant (157 studies [56.5%]). Few studies used clinical hypotony (3 isolated [1.1%]; 19 combined with low IOP [6.8%]). Forty-nine different criteria were found, with IOP < 6 mmHg, IOP < 6 mmHg on ≥ 2 consecutive visits after 3 months, and IOP < 5 mmHg being the most common (41 [14.7%], 38 [13.7%], and 13 [4.7%] studies, respectively). In both cohorts, numerical hypotony posed the highest risk of failure (HR, 1.51-1.21 for criteria A to D; P < 0.001), followed by mixed hypotony (HR, 1.41-1.20 for criteria A to D; P < 0.001), and clinical hypotony (HR, 1.12-1.04; P < 0.001). Failure risk varied greatly with various hypotony definitions, with the HR ranging from 1.02 to 10.79 for trabeculectomy and 1.00 to 8.36 for DS.

Conclusions

Hypotony failure criteria are highly heterogenous in the glaucoma literature, with few studies focusing on clinical manifestations. Numerical hypotony yields higher failure rates than clinical hypotony and can underestimate glaucoma surgery success rates. Standardizing failure criteria with an emphasis on clinically relevant hypotony manifestations is needed.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Mechanisms of blood-retinal barrier disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Mechanisms of blood-retinal barrier disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy.
content.abstract: Blood-retinal barrier (BRB) disruption is a common accompaniment of intermediate, posterior and panuveitis causing leakage into the retina and macular oedema resulting in vision loss. It is much less common in anterior uveitis or in patients with intraocular lymphoma who may have marked signs of intraocular inflammation. New drugs used for chemotherapy (cytarabine, immune checkpoint inhibitors, BRAF inhibitors, EGFR inhibitors, bispecific anti-EGFR inhibitors, MET receptor inhibitors and Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors) can also cause different types of uveitis and BRB disruption. As malignant disease itself can cause uveitis, particularly from breast, lung and gastrointestinal tract cancers, it can be clinically difficult to sort out the cause of BRB disruption. Immunosuppression due to malignant disease and/or chemotherapy can lead to infection which can also cause BRB disruption and intraocular infection. In this paper we address the pathophysiology of BRB disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy, methods for estimating the extent and effect of the disruption and examine why some types of intraocular inflammation and malignancy cause BRB disruption and others do not. Understanding this may help sort and manage these patients, as well as devise future therapeutic approaches.

records.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
content.abstract: Since the groundbreaking approval of the first anti-VEGF therapy in 2004, the retinal therapeutics field has undergone a remarkable transformation, witnessing a surge in novel, disease-modifying therapeutics for a broad spectrum of retinal diseases, extending beyond exudative VEGF-driven conditions. The surge in scientific advancement and the pressing, unmet, medical need have captured the attention of venture capital investors, who have collectively invested close to $10 billion in research and development of new retinal therapeutics between 2004 and 2023. Notably, the field of exudative diseases has gradually shifted away from trying to outcompete anti-VEGF therapeutics towards lowering the overall treatment burden by reducing injection frequency. Simultaneously, a new era has emerged in the non-exudative field, targeting prevalent conditions like dry AMD and rare indications such as Retinitis pigmentosa. This has led to promising drug candidates in development, culminating in the landmark approval of Luxturna for a rare form of Retinitis pigmentosa. The validation of new mechanisms, such as the complement pathway in dry AMD has paved the way for the approvals of Syvovre (Apellis) and Izervay (Iveric/Astellas), marking the first two therapies for this condition. In this comprehensive review, we share our view on the cumulative lessons from the past two decades in developing retinal therapeutics, covering both positive achievements and challenges. We also contextualize the investments, strategic partnering deals, and acquisitions of biotech companies, pharmaceutical companies venture capital investors in retinal therapeutics, respectively. Finally, we provide an outlook and potentially a forward-looking roadmap on novel retinal therapeutics, highlighting the emergence of potential new intervention strategies, such as cell-based therapies, gene editing, and combination therapies. We conclude that upcoming developments have the potential to further stimulate venture capital investments, which ultimately could facilitate the development and delivery of new therapies to patients in need.

records.title: Updated Guidelines for Imaging the Choriocapillaris in Eyes with Age-Related Macular Degeneration Using Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography.

content.title: Updated Guidelines for Imaging the Choriocapillaris in Eyes with Age-Related Macular Degeneration Using Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To update the recommended guidelines when quantifying choriocapillaris (CC) flow deficits (FDs) in eyes with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) using swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA).

Design

Evidence-based perspective.

Methods

Review of literature and experience of authors.

Results

A current challenge when quantifying CC FDs using SS-OCTA is the implementation of an objective compensation strategy to adjust for the signal attenuation arising under drusen in eyes with AMD. Our previous compensation strategy was used as a general approach to adjust for the OCTA signal attenuation associated with most drusen. However, the variability of the OCTA signal loss under drusen necessitated a more objective strategy that could be tailored to each case. We propose a compensation strategy using a parameter gamma (γ) that allows for the selection of an appropriate compensation level. The optimal γ value is identified as the one producing the most homogeneous OCT signal across the whole CC structural slab. This approach minimizes the possibility that areas of decreased flow in the compensated CC flow image might reflect drusen-related or compensation-related artifacts rather than true deficits. Additional lesions that present unique challenges when quantifying CC FDs include the presence of choroidal hypotransmission defects (hypoTDs) caused by calcified drusen and hyperreflective foci as well as choroidal hypertransmission defects (hyperTDs) caused by foci of atrophy. We recommend identifying and outlining these regions on an en face sub-retinal pigment epithelium (subRPE) slab with segmentation boundaries between 64 and 400 µm beneath the Bruch membrane (BM). The hypoTDs should be excluded from CC quantification because of the lack of significant OCTA signal, whereas the hyperTDs should be excluded from being compensated because doing so can artifactually increase the percentage of CC FDs.

Conclusions

The analysis of CC FDs in AMD requires special attention to drusen, hypoTDs, and hyperTDs to avoid introducing artifacts. By properly adjusting the compensation levels under drusen and adjusting the quantification of CC FDs by accounting for hyperTDs and hypoTDs, researchers interested in measuring CC FDs in AMD can have greater confidence in their measurements, particularly when investigating the role of CC flow impairment in AMD progression.

records.title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI)-Associated Retinal and Choroidal Adverse Reactions.

content.title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI)-Associated Retinal and Choroidal Adverse Reactions.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To summarize and categorize postulated mechanisms of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-mediated retinal and choroidal inflammation and discuss resulting implications for evaluation and management of these adverse reactions.

Design

Targeted literature review with interpretation and perspective METHODS: We performed a review of selected literature describing immune-mediated retinal and choroidal adverse reactions associated with ICI therapy, synthesizing and categorizing the likely underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Based on these mechanistic categories, we provide perspective on a rational approach to the evaluation of patients with ICI-associated inflammatory disorders of the retina and choroid.

Results

ICI-induced posterior segment adverse reactions can be categorized into 3 major mechanisms of unintended, targeted inflammation that share similarities to immunotherapy-related adverse events (irAEs) seen in other organ systems. In Type 1 reactions, T cell activation by ICIs can result in cross-reactivity of anti-tumor T cells with ocular tissues (Type 1a) or expansion of eye-specific T cells in predisposed individuals (Type 1b), leading to ocular inflammation that mimics known uveitic conditions. In Type 2 reactions, nonspecific ocular or systemic inflammation exacerbated by ICI use can cause retinal vasculitis through a "bystander" mechanism, potentially resulting in vision-threatening vascular occlusions. Finally, in Type 3 reactions, ICI use can prompt autoantibody-mediated inflammation and/or exacerbation of paraneoplastic processes likely related to T cell driven expansion of B cell populations.

Conclusions

Although relatively uncommon, posterior segment inflammatory disorders associated with systemic ICI therapy may be vision-threatening if not identified and treated appropriately. We propose that the pathogenic mechanisms underlying these chorioretinopathies falls into 3 major categories involving inadvertent T cell mediated inflammation. Visual prognosis with appropriate treatment is generally favorable, but some reactions, such as longstanding exudative retinal detachments and ICI-induced occlusive retinal vasculitis, can result in permanent visual defects.

records.title: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo) in the retina and implications for ocular diseases.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo) in the retina and implications for ocular diseases.
content.abstract: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo), formerly known as peripheral benzodiazepine receptor is a highly conserved transmembrane protein primarily located in the outer mitochondrial membrane. In the central nervous system (CNS), especially in glia cells, Tspo is upregulated upon inflammation. Consequently, Tspo was used as a tool for diagnostic in vivo imaging of neuroinflammation in the brain and as a potential therapeutic target. Several synthetic Tspo ligands have been explored as immunomodulatory and neuroprotective therapy approaches. Although the function of Tspo and how its ligands exert these beneficial effects is not fully clear, it became a research topic of interest, especially in ocular diseases in the past few years. This review summarizes state-of-the-art knowledge of Tspo expression and its proposed functions in different cells of the retina including microglia, retinal pigment epithelium and Müller cells. Tspo is involved in cytokine signaling, oxidative stress and reactive oxygen species production, calcium signaling, neurosteroid synthesis, energy metabolism, and cholesterol efflux. We also highlight recent developments in preclinical models targeting Tspo and summarize the relevance of Tspo biology for ocular and retinal diseases. We conclude that glial upregulation of Tspo in different ocular pathologies and the use of Tspo ligands as promising therapeutic approaches in preclinical studies underline the importance of Tspo as a potential disease-modifying protein.

records.title: Optical coherence tomography in the management of diabetic macular oedema.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Optical coherence tomography in the management of diabetic macular oedema.
content.abstract: Diabetic macular oedema (DMO) is the major cause of visual impairment in people with diabetes. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is now the most widely used modality to assess presence and severity of DMO. DMO is currently broadly classified based on the involvement to the central 1 mm of the macula into non-centre or centre involved DMO (CI-DMO) and DMO can occur with or without visual acuity (VA) loss. This classification forms the basis of management strategies of DMO. Despite years of research on quantitative and qualitative DMO related features assessed by OCT, these do not fully inform physicians of the prognosis and severity of DMO relative to visual function. Having said that, recent research on novel OCT biomarkers development and re-defined classification of DMO show better correlation with visual function and treatment response. This review summarises the current evidence of the association of OCT biomarkers in DMO management and its potential clinical importance in predicting VA and anatomical treatment response. The review also discusses some future directions in this field, such as the use of artificial intelligence to quantify and monitor OCT biomarkers and retinal fluid and identify phenotypes of DMO, and the need for standardisation and classification of OCT biomarkers to use in future clinical trials and clinical practice settings as prognostic markers and secondary treatment outcome measures in the management of DMO.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology-in the form of Machine Learning (ML) models and other models specialized in image recognition and processing, such as Convolutional Neural Networks Visual Transformers (CNN-ViTs)-is increasingly being used in ophthalmology. This review summarizes the main AI applications for laser-assisted refractive surgery. Methods: A wide-ranging literature search on the PubMed and ISI Thompson Web of Science databases was conducted. Results: AI is an all-encompassing technological concept that refers to either specific applications of ML/CNN models, such as in keratoconus screening or diagnosis, or agentic/multimodal AI applications that process different data types using a variety of AI models. The most clinically established applications found were corneal ectasia and keratoconus screening, in which AI models can reliably exceed 95% diagnostic accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity; nomogram-derived laser ablation programming; optimization of ray-tracing calculations for ray-traced ablation profiles; patient screening and selection for refractive surgery; visual and refractive result prediction; assessment of postoperative corneal ectasia risk; detection of intraoperative complications; research on the laser coupling effect; and other applications such as monitoring eye rubbing behavior in corneal ectasia suspects. Thus, singular, specific applications of AI models have made the largest clinical contributions. These results must be interpreted with a comparison of internal versus external validation, calibration, and generalizability. Overall the technology is highly promising. Agentic/multimodal AI frameworks are currently being discussed, with pilot studies published and applicability proposed in the context of large, high-patient-volume clinical practices. The technological advent of SHAP force plot graphs and saliency maps has improved understanding of the factors that contribute mechanistically to AI model reasoning, leading to more informed clinical decisions or research applicability, such as in finding parameters or factors linked to postoperative ectasia. Conclusions: AI is already established in laser-assisted refractive surgery in the form of models specialized in data-intensive analysis. At present, the best-performing novel AI models originate from the domain of large or multi-hospital settings due to requirements for multiple latest-generation diagnostic devices, high-volume patient data, computing expertise, and resources. Future directions could include clinical standardization and trickle-down dissemination of the technology. Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Agentic/multimodal AI implementation is offset by challenges in complexity, the technological limitations of LLMs ("hallucinations"), and ethical and legislative factors.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

content.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
content.abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis explains the histological pattern of injury seen through light microscopy in kidney biopsy specimens and is the end result of different injuries to podocytes. The clinical classification of patients by FSGS lesion is challenging because of a broad spectrum of etiologies, limited understanding of pathophysiology, and poor correlation among histopathology, treatment response, and clinical outcomes. Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is a problematic process to detect lesions, with low and late analysis of the absence of initial symptoms, and a challenging position of specific markers. However, Histopathological and genomic Data in Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) are significantly used in multiple research applications, but they face several limitations that restrict the efficiency of experimental analysis. This review systematically analyzed recent enhancements in biopsy-based analysis and deep learning models for FSGS, with specific emphasis on different mechanisms. Moreover, this review analyzed different strategies, namely kidney transplantation, pathogenesis to therapeutic approaches, transformer-based architectures, glomerular segmentation methodologies, multitasking strategy classification, and gene expression analysis for FSGS. This review analysis includes 121 research papers, which are selected and analyzed for glomerular segmentation, gene expression, clinical outcomes, lesion classification, and disease recurrence prediction. Based on the recent research frameworks, it explicitly states the performance analysis, benefits, as well as challenges of FSGS. The article presents details of a new dataset and future directions for improving the majority of nephropathology diagnoses previously available through the use of integrated approaches that utilize both histopathology and genomics, enhancing future research direction in FSGS.

records.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI), mainly AI-driven chatbots and large language models (LLMs) is reshaping dental education through adaptive, interactive, and simulation-based learning. While the transition in technology has been rapid, the evidence about the educational effectiveness of these technologies is still very diverse and not entirely directed.

Aim

To analyze the roles, educational effectiveness, and impact of integrating AI-driven chatbots and LLMs in dental education at the university level with a focus on learning outcomes and implementation practices.

Methods

The researchers conducted a thorough search of the electronic databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for articles published from January 2018 to November 2025. This review met the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 criteria and was made up of original research articles on dental studentsand educators who were using AI-based chatbots as interventions. The outcomes measured were knowledge gain, clinical reasoning, diagnostic accuracy, communication skills, and engagement of learners. Due to the differences in the methodologies used the authors opted for a narrative synthesis approach.

Results

Six studies met the eligibility criteria and showed potential benefits of AI-driven chatbots and LLMs for diagnostic reasoning, learning performance, engagement, and individualized feedback although methodological and outcome heterogeneity limited direct comparison.

Conclusion

AI-driven chatbots and LLMs may complement university-level dental education, but their effectiveness and safe implementation require further rigorous evaluation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence applications in biofilm research: computational approaches for biofilm analysis and antimicrobial prediction.

content.title: Artificial intelligence applications in biofilm research: computational approaches for biofilm analysis and antimicrobial prediction.
content.abstract: Biofilms are organized groups of microbes surrounded by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix. This structure helps microbes survive, creates metabolic differences, and makes them less sensitive to antimicrobial treatments. Because biofilms can block antimicrobials and help microbes adapt, they often cause chronic and recurring infections that are hard to treat with standard methods. Most current diagnostic and antimicrobial testing methods focus on free-floating (planktonic) microbes and do not reflect the complex structure and behavior of mature biofilms. This gap often leads to ongoing treatment failures and poor predictions of treatment outcomes. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and computational modeling have shown promise for improving biofilm research. These tools can help with automated detection, structural analysis, computational phenotyping, and predicting how biofilms will respond to treatments. This review examines current and emerging AI-based methods in biofilm biology, focusing on computational analysis, prediction of antimicrobial responses, and AI-supported antibiofilm therapies. It also discusses challenges such as dataset differences, limited real-world testing, difficulty understanding models, and a lack of models for clinically important mixed-species biofilms. Overall, this review shows how AI could help improve the accuracy, integration, and tailoring of biofilm research and antimicrobial management.

records.title: Effectiveness of the flipped classroom in medical education: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness of the flipped classroom in medical education: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the FC approach compared to conventional teaching methods in medical education.

Methods

A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases was conducted. Eighteen eligible studies, involving diverse learner populations, were included in the analysis. The effectiveness of the FC model was assessed across five predefined domains: theoretical knowledge, procedural/technical skills, self-directed learning ability, case analysis/problem-solving ability, and learner satisfaction.

Results

Pooled analyses demonstrated significant advantages of the FC model, with moderate to large effect sizes observed across most outcomes. Notable improvements were found in self-directed learning ability and procedural/technical skills. Subgroup analyses suggested that residents showed larger benefits, particularly in procedural/technical skills and learner satisfaction. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the direction of the findings, although statistical significance was not retained in all leave-one-out analyses for some outcomes.

Conclusions

Flipped classrooms were associated with improved outcomes in medical education, with larger effects in residents. Given high heterogeneity and limited evidence in some domains, benefits appear context dependent. Implementation should be tailored, and future studies should define mechanisms and optimal conditions.

records.title: The impact of non-invasive brain stimulation and digital intervention on social cognitive therapy in autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: The impact of non-invasive brain stimulation and digital intervention on social cognitive therapy in autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Introduction

To evaluate the relative efficacy of non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) and digital interventions for improving social cognition in autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane, CNKI to February 2026 yielded 50 randomized controlled trials (RCTs). A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed using R, ranking interventions via Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking curve (SUCRA) and assessing evidence certainty with Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINEMA).

Results

Across the included trials (mean age range: 2.54 to 20.80 years), among 9 interventions, transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) emerged as optimal (SUCRA = 88.24%), significantly outperforming treatment as usual (TAU) (SMD=-1.69, 95% CrI: -2.67, -0.70). This was followed by high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) (84.38%, SMD=-1.60, 95% CrI: -2.32, -0.89), low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (LF-rTMS) (74.22%, SMD=-1.36, 95% CrI: -1.77, -0.96), and theta-burst stimulation (TBS) (64.21%, SMD=-1.19, 95% CrI: -2.02, -0.35); all significantly outperformed TAU. Standalone digital interventions ranked lower. Meta-regression showed no significant age moderating effect.

Conclusions

tDCS is the most efficacious standalone intervention for ASD social cognitive deficits. We recommend tDCS or TBS clinically and advocate a synergistic paradigm integrating NIBS neural priming with digital training. However, future large-scale, rigorous RCTs are required to further validate both these standalone modalities and the proposed combined protocols.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261337491, identifier CRD420261337491.

records.title: AI-driven biosensing technology for early disease detection: A comprehensive review.
records.publisher: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

content.title: AI-driven biosensing technology for early disease detection: A comprehensive review.
content.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is quickly changing the field of biosensing technologies to the point of early, real-time, and individualized disease detection and overcoming significant drawbacks of traditional biosensors, including noise interference, signal drift, and inability to process non-linear biological data.ObjectiveThis review examines the latest developments in AI-driven biosensing systems and assess their impact on diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.MethodsThis critical review focuses on recently published works (2021-2025) on AI-integrated biosensing platforms, such as optical, electrochemical, wearable, and nanomaterial-based platforms, and machine learning, deep learning, edge AI, multimodal data fusion, and federated learning. Results: CNNs and LSTMs, Transformers and ensemble learning are advanced AI models with better sensitivity, specificity, automatic extraction of features, and prediction accuracy of critical diseases like cancer, cardiovascular, infectious, neurological, and metabolic diseases. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), nano-enabled biosensors, digital twins, and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) are examples of emerging technologies and ideas that are improving real-time, dependable, customized, and privacy-preserving diagnostic systems.ConclusionThe change to proactive and predictive healthcare is being facilitated by AI-enhanced biosensing. It has a good chance in early diagnosis, better treatment planning as well as the decrease in healthcare expenses. Nevertheless, there are still challenges such as lack of data, generalization of models, regulatory authorization, and moral issues.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of the JAK1 inhibitor abrocitinib for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of the JAK1 inhibitor abrocitinib for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory disease with substantial pruritic burden. Abrocitinib, an oral selective Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibitor, targets cytokine pathways central to AD pathophysiology. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated its efficacy and safety in moderate-to-severe AD.

Methods

Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidance, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched to 21 August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing abrocitinib with placebo. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane RoB 2.0). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; model choice was based on heterogeneity.

Results

Five double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs involving 1,927 patients were included. Abrocitinib significantly improved Investigator's Global Assessment response (RR = 2.97, 95% CI: 2.45-3.60), Eczema Area and Severity Index-75 response (RR = 2.56, 95% CI: 2.25-2.92), and ≥4-point Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale improvement (RR = 2.64, 95% CI: 2.29-3.06), with greater efficacy observed for 200 mg than 100 mg. Treatment-emergent adverse events were increased (RR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.10-1.27), mainly nausea (RR = 5.53, 95% CI: 3.41-9.34). Headache was also increased overall (RR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.16-2.47), whereas skin allergy was reduced (RR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.44-0.82).

Conclusion

Abrocitinib provides clinically meaningful short-term improvements in disease severity and pruritus in moderate-to-severe AD. The 200 mg dose offers greater efficacy but requires careful monitoring for tolerability, particularly nausea and headache.

records.title: Levosimendan vs. Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Levosimendan vs. Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

To compare the clinical efficacy and safety of intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) and levosimendan in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed®, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted through July 2024. Outcomes analyzed included atrial fibrillation, postoperative mediastinitis, the requirement for inotropic support, in-hospital mortality, postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) stay, postoperative length of stay, ventilation time, and mean arterial pressure (MAP) levels.

Results

The analysis included nine studies with 681 patients. Levosimendan presented advantage over IABP in CABG patients in terms of postoperative ICU stay, postoperative length of stay, and reduction in MAP levels, with effect sizes: mean difference (MD) = -0.83, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.97 to -0.68, P < 0.00001, MD = -1.14, 95% CI: -1.33 to -0.95, P < 0.00001, and MD = -4.55, 95% CI: -6.14 to -2.96, P < 0.00001, respectively. Levosimendan had an advantage on subgroup analyses in terms of postoperative ICU stay and postoperative length of stay, with effect sizes: MD = -0.83, 95% CI: -0.93 to -0.72, P < 0.00001 and MD = -1.14, 95% CI: -1.28 to -1.01, P < 0.00001, respectively. However, the incidence of postoperative mediastinitis was higher in the levosimendan group (relative risk = 1.45, 95% CI: 0.88 to 2.38), though not statistically significant.

Conclusion

Levosimendan may improve recovery and hemodynamic outcomes in high-risk CABG patients compared to IABP but may be associated with a higher, though non-significant, risk of mediastinitis. Further high-quality studies are warranted.

records.title: Clinical utility of LLMs in otology and neurotology: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

content.title: Clinical utility of LLMs in otology and neurotology: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for patient education and clinical decision support in otolaryngology. However, their reliability varies across clinical tasks, and their performance in otology and neurotology, where decision-making often requires integration of complex audiological, vestibular, and imaging data, remains unclear.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Eligibility criteria were defined using the Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes, Timing, and Setting (PICOTS) framework. The primary outcome was overall LLM accuracy. Secondary outcomes included agreement with experts, hallucination rate, safety, readability, reproducibility, and task-specific performance. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled accuracy.

Results

Forty-one studies were included, with 31 contributing to the meta-analysis. GPT-based LLMs achieved a pooled accuracy of 73.5% (95% CI, 64.5%-80.8%), significantly outperforming non-GPT LLMs (56.5%; 95% CI, 43.2%-68.9%; p = 0.029). Performance varied by task type, with the highest accuracy for patient education (83.5%) and the lowest for diagnosis (54.6%) and treatment recommendations (57.9%). Although substantial heterogeneity was observed, formal assessment did not provide clear evidence of small-study effects, although these analyses should be interpreted cautiously.

Conclusion

GPT-based LLMs show promise for patient education and knowledge-based tasks in otology and neurotology. However, their limited performance in diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making supports their use as adjuncts rather than replacements for clinician judgment.

records.title: Prevalence of cognitive frailty in older adults with stroke in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Prevalence of cognitive frailty in older adults with stroke in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Stroke is a leading cause of disability and mortality in older adults. Post-stroke cognitive frailty (CF) increases the risk of adverse outcomes. However, evidence regarding the prevalence of CF remains limited and inconsistent. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prevalence of CF among older adults with stroke in China and identifies factors associated with variation in prevalence, thereby informing future research directions and potential clinical considerations.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China Biomedical Literature Database (CBM), China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Database, and Wanfang Database for relevant studies reporting the prevalence of CF in Chinese older adults with stroke. The search covered the period from each database's inception to November 2024. Eligible studies were assessed for quality, and data were extracted. All analyses were performed using Stata 18.0 software.

Results

Four Chinese studies involving 1,337 participants were included. Meta-analysis revealed a pooled prevalence of CF among older adults with stroke of 33% (95% CI: 28-39%). Subgroup analysis indicated a significantly higher prevalence of CF in stroke patients aged ≥80 years compared to those aged 60-79 years (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the prevalence was significantly higher among those who consumed alcohol than among non-consumers (p < 0.05). Notably, subgroup estimates for patients with malnutrition and depression were markedly high, at 47% (95% CI: 34-60%) and 62% (95% CI: 53-71%), respectively.

Conclusion

Available evidence suggests that the prevalence of CF among older adults with stroke in China appears to be substantial, with significant variations associated with alcohol consumption and advanced age. The particularly high prevalence estimates in patients with malnutrition or depression warrant increased clinical attention and further investigation into their relationship with post-stroke CF. Caution is warranted given the limited evidence base (n = 4), high heterogeneity, and exclusively hospital-based Chinese setting; larger studies are needed to confirm these observations. Early identification and evidence-based interventions targeting CF in this population may be crucial to mitigating adverse health outcomes pending further validation.

Systematic review registration

This systematic review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42025643159).

records.title: AI-Driven Predictive Models of Early Recurrence of HCC After Surgical Resection: A Systematic Review.

content.title: AI-Driven Predictive Models of Early Recurrence of HCC After Surgical Resection: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early recurrence after curative-intent resection is a major determinant of poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive models have emerged to identify patients at high risk of recurrence but remain incompletely synthesized for early recurrence specifically. This review aimed to identify and appraise AI-driven models predicting early recurrence after surgical resection. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to November 2025. Eligible studies developed and evaluated AI-driven models predicting early recurrence (≤24 months) after curative-intent hepatectomy as first-line treatment for HCC. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST+AI, and findings were synthesized narratively due to methodological heterogeneity. The review was registered in PROSPERO. Results: Thirty-six studies involving 14,716 patients were included. Most studies originated from China (33/36, 91.7%), were single-center (27/36, 75%), and retrospective (35/36, 97.2%). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was the predominant imaging modality (15/36, 41.7%), followed by computed tomography (CT) (11/36, 30.6%) and ultrasound (US)/contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) (6/36, 16.7%). Three studies developed non-imaging models, and one combined CT and MRI. In within-study comparisons, multimodal models generally showed better discrimination than unimodal approaches. Peritumoral, habitat-based, and multiphasic strategies appeared promising. However, external validation was reported in only 6/36 studies (16.7%), calibration and decision-curve analysis were inconsistently reported, and most studies had high risk of bias. Conclusions: AI-driven models show potential to predict early recurrence of HCC after curative-intent resection. Nevertheless, evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and restricted geographical diversity, while clinical utility remains inconsistently evaluated, and no model has yet been generalized in clinical practice. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized outcomes, transparent reporting, and external validation are needed for clinical implementation.

records.title: Effect of histology on the efficacy of first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effect of histology on the efficacy of first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

First-line immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become the standard of care for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, whether tumor histology influences the efficacy of ICIs remains unclear.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to February 28, 2026. Eligible studies compared ICIs with chemotherapy, or two ICI-based regimens, as first-line treatment for advanced squamous (SQ) or non-squamous (non-SQ) NSCLC. Trials that enrolled patients with NSCLC and reported outcomes stratified by histology were also eligible. The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% credible intervals. A fixed-effects consistency model was used for the statistical analysis.

Results

Forty-one phase 3 RCTs comprising 23, 871 patients and 31 ICI-based regimens were included. The efficacy of individual ICI regimens varied by histological subtype. For example, toripalimab plus chemotherapy was associated with superior OS compared with most other ICI regimens (HR range: 0.42-0.65) and ranked as the best treatment in non-SQ-NSCLC (surface under the cumulative ranking curve [SUCRA] = 0.97). In contrast, the same regimen showed inferior OS relative to many comparators (HR range for comparators vs. toripalimab plus chemotherapy: 0.47-0.65) and had the lowest OS ranking in SQ-NSCLC (SUCRA = 0.09). In the PD-L1 < 1% subgroup, nivolumab plus ipilimumab demonstrated a trend toward better OS compared with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy (HR = 0.59) and ranked as the best regimen for SQ-NSCLC (SUCRA = 0.83), whereas pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy provided the greatest OS benefit for non-SQ-NSCLC (SUCRA = 0.90). In the PD-L1 ≥ 50% subgroup, atezolizumab plus chemotherapy ranked second for OS benefit in SQ-NSCLC but was the least effective combination in non-SQ-NSCLC; conversely, cemiplimab plus chemotherapy was the least effective combination in SQ-NSCLC but ranked second in non-SQ-NSCLC.

Conclusions

The efficacy of individual first-line ICI regimens appear to vary by histological subtype across PD-L1 expression levels. These findings suggest that PD-L1 status alone might not be sufficient to guide treatment selection, and that histological subtype could be considered in clinical decision-making for advanced NSCLC.

records.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of physical rehabilitation on functional recovery in critically ill patients.

content.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of physical rehabilitation on functional recovery in critically ill patients.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Survivors of critical illness frequently experience persistent physical impairment, particularly ICU-acquired weakness (ICU-AW), which contributes to prolonged disability after intensive care. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effects of physical rehabilitation on muscle strength, physical function, health-related quality of life, and clinical outcomes in critically ill adults.

Methods

Four electronic databases were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing physical rehabilitation with usual rehabilitation in adult critically ill patients were included. The primary outcome was muscle strength assessed by the Medical Research Council (MRC) sum score. Secondary outcomes included ICU-AW, physical function, health-related quality of life, duration of mechanical ventilation (MV), mortality, and ICU and hospital length of stay.

Results

Forty RCTs involving 5,135 patients (2,554 physical rehabilitation; 2,581 usual rehabilitation) were included. Physical rehabilitation was associated with improved MRC sum score (SMD 0.26, 95% CI 0.05-0.46; p = 0.02; I 2 = 70%), reduced incidence of ICU-AW (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.87; p = 0.007; I 2 = 34%), improved Barthel Index (SMD 0.62, 95% CI 0.21-1.03; p = 0.003; I 2 = 85%) and SF-36 physical function (SMD 0.53, 95% CI 0.26-0.81; p < 0.001; I 2 = 81%), shortened duration of MV (MD -1.32 days, 95% CI -1.98 to -0.65; p < 0.001; I 2 = 66%) and ICU length of stay (MD -1.41 days, 95% CI -2.03 to -0.78; p < 0.001; I 2 = 44%), but had no significant effects on mortality or hospital length of stay.

Conclusion

Physical rehabilitation is associated with improved muscle strength and functional recovery, reduced ICU-AW, and shorter mechanical ventilation duration and ICU stay, but not reduced mortality. Further high-quality Multicenter trials are needed to define the optimal rehabilitation strategy.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023462649, Identifier CRD42023462649.

records.title: Application of machine learning and deep learning in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Application of machine learning and deep learning in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) can progress to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis, contributing to a heavier global health burden. Non-invasive diagnostic tools developed using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), two representative artificial intelligence algorithms, are increasingly being explored for MASH and its related fibrosis assessment.

Objectives

This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of different ML and DL models and identify the top-performing models for diagnosing MASH and associated liver fibrosis.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, Embase and Cochrane Library from inception to May 18, 2025. Pooled area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUROC) values with 95 % confidence interval (CI) were calculated. Accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, positive predictive values, and negative predictive values were also recorded.

Results

Of 4,314 studies initially identified, 106 met the inclusion criteria, with 35 studies (ML: n = 28; DL: n = 7) providing data for analysis. Logistic Regression and Neural Network are the most commonly algorithms applied in ML and DL, respectively. The pooled AUROCs for diagnosing MASH were 0.833 (95 %CI: 0.806-0.860) for ML models and 0.841 (95 %CI: 0.782-0.900) for DL models. Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) and ResNet50 were the best-performing models for diagnosing MASH within ML and DL algorithms, respectively, achieving corresponding AUROCs of 0.920 (95 %CI: 0.916-0.924) and 0.960 (95 %CI: 0.951-0.969). For fibrosis diagnosis, ML models had a pooled AUROC of 0.826 (95 %CI: 0.792-0.860), with Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) achieving the highest AUROC of 0.960 (95 %CI: 0.950-0.970). DL models yielded the pooled AUROC of 0.875 (95 %CI: 0.816-0.934) for fibrosis diagnosis.

Conclusions

Both ML and DL models demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for MASH and liver fibrosis, with DL achieving marginally higher AUROCs. AI-driven approaches show promise in MASLD management.

records.title: The effects of Tai Chi on executive function and neurophysiological outcomes in college students: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The effects of Tai Chi on executive function and neurophysiological outcomes in college students: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

College students face substantial cognitive demands, motivating scalable non-pharmacological approaches to support executive function. Tai Chi combines low-to-moderate physical activity, motor-sequence learning, postural control, breathing regulation, and sustained attention, but evidence in young adults remains uncertain.

Objective

To evaluate the effects of Tai Chi on objective executive-function outcomes and to summarize associated neurophysiological findings in university students.

Methods

Following PRISMA 2020, PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and CNKI were searched from inception to 15 April 2026, with an English-language restriction. Eligible studies evaluated structured Tai Chi against a concurrent comparator and reported objective executive-function and/or prespecified neurophysiological outcomes. Two reviewers screened records, extracted data, and assessed randomized trials using RoB 2. Certainty was evaluated using GRADE. Hedges' g was pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; REML and Hartung-Knapp analyses assessed robustness. The present review was not prospectively registered; PROSPERO CRD420261480624 concerns a future update.

Results

Seven randomized trials were eligible (n = 425), and four comparisons entered the primary selected-task meta-analysis (n = 248). The pooled estimate favored Tai Chi (g = 1.05, 95% CI 0.23-1.87; i 2 = 89.0%) but was dominated by one task-congruent working-memory trial and was not robust under Hartung-Knapp inference (95% CI - 0.56 to 2.67; p = 0.130). Inhibitory-control performance improved across three trials (n = 193; g = 0.57, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; i 2 = 0%), although certainty was low. Working memory effects were nonsignificant for the primary selected metric (g = 1.00, 95% CI - 0.37 to 2.37) and correct responses/accuracy (g = 0.79, 95% CI - 0.19 to 1.77). Cognitive flexibility was represented by one trial (g = 0.29, 95% CI - 0.20 to 0.77). Neurophysiological findings were exploratory. No study reported objective academic outcomes.

Conclusion

Tai Chi may improve short-term inhibitory-control performance in college students, but evidence for broader executive-function benefits is insufficient. Larger preregistered trials using active comparators, task-neutral measures, longer follow-up, and objective academic outcomes are required.

records.title: The primary preventive effect of sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitors on chronic kidney disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The primary preventive effect of sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitors on chronic kidney disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Aim

To assess the efficacy of Sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitors (SGLTis) in the primary prevention (PP) of chronic kidney disease (CKD) among patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D).

Method

Literature was retrieved from MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases up to January 1, 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or their subgroups and observational studies involving T2D patients without CKD treated with SGLTis for ≥ 1 year, focusing on CKD-related composite outcomes. Seven articles meeting inclusion criteria were included. The hazard ratio (RR) was calculated, and the degree of heterogeneity was assessed. Subsequently, 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) were computed accordingly.

Result

In RCTs, 15,228 eligible participants received SGLTis and 12,736 received placebo. Meta-analysis using random-effects models showed that SGLTis reduced CKD-related composite outcomes by 53% (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.39, 0.57; P < 0.0001) with low heterogeneity (I² = 6%).
